title: Breakout 3D with Save/Load State
prompt:
Create a single HTML file implementing a 3D Breakout game with save/load state functionality using Three.js and GLTFLoader.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 25, 30) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light from (10, 20, 10) with intensity 1.0.
- The play field is a rectangular 3D arena: width=20, depth=30, centered at origin. Create visible walls (left, right, back) as thin box geometries (color: #555555). The bottom edge (near camera) is open — that's where the ball can escape.
- Load the 'robot.glb' model using GLTFLoader. Scale it to roughly 1.5 units tall. Place it at the center-back of the arena as a decorative trophy/target behind the bricks. It should slowly rotate on Y axis (0.5 rad/s).

## Bricks
- Create a grid of 5 rows x 6 columns of bricks. Each brick is a BoxGeometry(2.8, 0.8, 1.2). Position them in the upper half of the arena (z from -12 to -4), centered on X. Color rows differently: row0=#ff0000, row1=#ff8800, row2=#ffff00, row3=#00ff00, row4=#0088ff. Each brick has a `hit` property, initially false.

## Paddle
- A BoxGeometry(4, 0.5, 1) paddle at z=12, y=0.25, colored #ffffff. Player moves it left/right with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight keys (speed: 15 units/sec). Clamp paddle X to [-8, 8].

## Ball
- A SphereGeometry(0.4) ball, color #ff00ff. Starts at (0, 0.4, 10) with velocity (5, 0, -8) units/sec. The ball moves in the XZ plane at y=0.4.
- Ball bounces off left wall (x=-10), right wall (x=10), back wall (z=-15). When hitting the paddle (check z and x overlap), reflect Z velocity. When hitting a brick, mark it hit=true, hide it, reflect Z velocity, and increment score.
- If ball z > 14 (past paddle), it's a miss: decrement lives, reset ball to (0, 0.4, 10) with velocity (5, 0, -8), set gameRunning to false (pause until Space pressed).

## Game State
- Start with lives=3, score=0, gameRunning=false. Press Space to start/resume.
- Display HUD with: Score, Lives, and two buttons 'Save State' (id='saveBtn') and 'Load State' (id='loadBtn').

## Save/Load
- 'Save State' button: serialize current ball position, ball velocity, paddle position, score, lives, each brick's hit status, and gameRunning into a JSON object stored in window.__savedState and also localStorage key 'breakout3d_save'.
- 'Load State' button: restore all the above from window.__savedState (or localStorage). Update all 3D objects to match. Set window.__3D_STATE__.lastLoadTime = Date.now().

## window.__3D_STATE__ must expose:
- score (number)
- lives (number)
- gameRunning (boolean)
- ballPosition: {x, y, z}
- ballVelocity: {x, y, z}
- paddleX (number)
- bricksRemaining (number, count of bricks not hit)
- totalBricks (number, always 30)
- robotLoaded (boolean, true once GLB loads)
- robotRotationY (number, current Y rotation of robot)
- savedStateExists (boolean, true if window.__savedState is defined)
- lastLoadTime (number or 0)

Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.

## Physics
- Use simple AABB collision for bricks and paddle.
- Ball speed magnitude should remain roughly constant (between 8 and 12 units/sec). After each bounce, normalize velocity to magnitude 9.4.
- Delta time clamped to max 0.05s to prevent tunneling.
physics_constraints: Ball moves in XZ plane at fixed Y. Bounces off walls, paddle, bricks with velocity reflection. Speed normalized to ~9.4 after bounces. Ball resets on miss (z>14). Delta time clamped to 0.05s.
